title: Lecture 5 · Partitioning
outline:
STATUS: complete. Helpers (common.js, common-2.js, common-3.js) written, linted and visually tested; ds-5.html, audio stub and 11 placeholder scenes in place; node tools/video-still.js ds-5 info shows the total.

Lecture 5 video (Data Science COM3021, 'Partitioning'): 11 scenes, 121.5 s: title (4), copies do not fit so split the data (12), key ranges (12), the timestamp trap (12.5), hash partitioning (13), the price of hashing: range queries (11.5), secondary index by document (11.5), by term (12), rebalancing: mod N versus fixed partitions (13.5), dynamic partitions split and merge (10.5), recap (9). Story: copies do not fit when data outgrows a node, so split it into partitions, each item in exactly one, and copy each partition to another node (scene 2, lesson 5.1); key-range partitioning gives each node a range of sorted keys: neighbours stay together so a range query reads one node (3, 5.2), but with a timestamp key every new write hits the one node that owns 'now' (4, 5.2); hash partitioning gives each node a range of hash values so keys spread evenly (5, 5.3) at the price of scattering range queries over all nodes (6, 5.3); a secondary index (search by colour) either lives in each partition (by document: the search is scattered to every partition, a write touches one: 7) or is itself split by term (one index partition answers a search, but a write updates several: 8) (5.4); when a node joins, 'key mod N' moves 9 of 12 keys but fixed partitions move only 3 whole partitions (9), and dynamic partitions split past a size limit and merge when small (10) (5.5). Not covered: compound keys, replication details beyond leader/follower, the workshop 5.W itself (the recap points to it).

LESSONS the facts come from: ds5-why 5.1, ds5-range 5.2, ds5-hash 5.3, ds5-index 5.4, ds5-rebalance 5.5, ds5-cluster 5.W and boss ds5-boss (Parcelo, not used); js/content/ds/ds-l5-01.js, ds-l5-02.js, ds-l5-03.js, ds-l5-workshop.js.

EXAMPLE DATA (all asserted at page load by videos/d5/common.js; a wrong number throws an Error): scene 2: 12 orders, 4 nodes, room for 8; full copies need 12 per node (4 too many); split 3 per node; with a follower of the previous node's partition each node holds 6. Scene 3: ranges A-F, G-M, N-S, T-Z; names Adams Chen Evans | Jones Khan Lewis Morgan | Nolan Patel Quinn | Taylor Usman Young; Okafor goes to N-S between Nolan and Patel; Khan to Mills touches only G-M (Khan, Lewis). Scene 4: hour ranges 00-05, 06-11, 12-17, 18-23; writes 14:02 14:09 14:13 14:21 14:34 14:50 all land on node 3 (loads 0, 0, 6, 0). Scenes 5-6: ids 101-116 with toy hashes 11 2 14 6 9 0 13 4 7 15 1 10 5 12 3 8; hash ranges 0-3, 4-7, 8-11, 12-15 per node; keys 101-108 land on nodes 3 1 4 2 3 1 4 2 (two each); key-range layout 101-104 | 105-108 | 109-112 | 113-116; a query for ids 101-104 asks 1 node with ranges, 4 with hashing. Scenes 7-8: 12 cars (1 red ford, 2 blue kia, 3 green mini, 4 red kia, 5 blue ford, 6 red mini, 7 green ford, 8 blue mini, 9 red ford, 10 green kia, 11 blue kia, 12 red mini) in 3 document partitions by id mod 3; red cars 1 4 6 9 12 (partition 2 has none); index partitions blue+ford, green+kia, mini+red; saving car 13 (blue mini) updates index partitions 1 and 3 plus its document partition. Scene 9: 12 keys on 3 nodes, key mod 3 -> key mod 4 moves keys 3-11 (9) and keeps 0-2; 12 fixed partitions p mod 3, node D steals P9, P10, P11 (3 moves) leaving [0,3,6] [1,4,7] [2,5,8] [9,10,11]. Scene 10: partitions 6, 8, 4 GB +4 each = 10, 12, 8; the 12 splits into 6 + 6 (limit 10 GB); halving gives 5, 3, 3, 4 and the two 3s merge into 6.

VIDEO-WIDE CONVENTIONS: COLOURS (whole video): blue = the data and what we ask about (keys, orders, records, the query, the search word); green = even, fits, cheap, healthy (a fair node, a tick, 'asked 1 node'); red = overload, overflow, hot spot, expensive ('asked 4 nodes', 'moved 9 of 12'); orange = attention and things in motion (the new node, the key being placed, a pointer, a hashed number, a stolen partition); purple = the routing rule or lookup table (range tags, hash ranges, the hash box, the index, 'key mod N', the size limit); grey = neutral (idle nodes, empty slots, the rest). Every label is 28 px or more; symbols are SVG (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, D5.icon.*), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure). Setup lines every scene starts with: const V = window.VID, D5 = V.d5, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. Shared layout: the cluster rig (D5.cluster) is the same sticker everywhere: a grey server card with a header (server icon + 'Node N') and a grid of dashed slots; chips (blue) are the data. Four-node scenes use x 12, w 210, gap 24; the three-node scenes use w 288, gap 24. Data is reused: scenes 5 and 6 share the 16 ids and the hash table; scenes 7 and 8 share the 12 cars and the three document partitions; scenes 3 and 4 share the key-range idea (surnames, then hours). The caption rule: a caption never runs ahead of its picture. Captions are sentences of at most about 20 characters per second. Title card kicker 'Data Science · Lecture 5' (like the other series).

title: Copies do not fit,
so split the data
caps: Twelve orders. Each node has room for eight.
A full copy on every node does not fit.
So split them: each order lives in one partition.
Each partition is also copied to another node.
scenes.spec:
IDEA (lesson ds5-why 5.1): replication copies the whole dataset to every node, which fails when the data is too big; partitioning gives each node a different subset (a partition), each order in exactly one; real systems also keep a copy (follower) of each partition on another node. Data: D5.SPLIT (12 orders, 4 nodes, room for 8), D5.layout('rep'|'part'|'both') gives the chips every node holds (rep: 12 each = 4 too many; part: 3 each; both: 6 each, which fits). COLOURS (whole video): blue = the data and what we ask about (keys, orders, records, the query, the search word); green = even, fits, cheap, healthy (a fair node, a tick, 'asked 1 node'); red = overload, overflow, hot spot, expensive ('asked 4 nodes', 'moved 9 of 12'); orange = attention and things in motion (the new node, the key being placed, a pointer, a hashed number, a stolen partition); purple = the routing rule or lookup table (range tags, hash ranges, the hash box, the index, 'key mod N', the size limit); grey = neutral (idle nodes, empty slots, the rest). Every label is 28 px or more; symbols are SVG (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, D5.icon.*), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure). Setup lines every scene starts with: const V = window.VID, D5 = V.d5, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V.

LAYOUT (stage px). Nodes: const cl = D5.cluster(stage, {x: 12, y: 250, n: 4, w: 210, gap: 24, cols: 4, rows: 2, cw: 44, ch: 44, cg: 6}) (node card 250-416, eight dashed slots = the room for 8; slot(n, 8..11) is a third row of four slots hanging BELOW the card at y about 436: the overflow). Purple partition tags over the nodes via cl.set(n, {tag: 'P1'..'P4'}) (tag centred on the 58 px above the card). Orders: 12 blue chips D5.chip(stage, {text: '1'..'12', w: 44, h: 44}) in a tray at y 70, centre x = 160 + 56 i, with a blue D5.tag(stage, {x: 383, y: 0, w: 170, text: '12 orders', tone: 'blue'}) above it. Replication copies: 48 extra chips (12 per node), tone blue for orders 1-8 and tone red + solid for 9-12 (overflow). Per-node fit tags 'x of 8' (D5.tag, 28 px, green) at y 440 under each node. Legend at y 520-578: a solid blue chip + tag 'leader' at x 250, a dashed blue chip (dashed: true) + tag 'follower' at x 520.

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.0 the four nodes pop (k, 0.08 s apart) and the 12 tray chips pop (D5.appear, 0.05 s apart from 0.3); the 'room for 8' fact is the eight dashed slots. 2.8-4.6 REPLICATION: for every node, copies of orders 1..12 fly (D5.fly, arc -30, E.inOut, 0.9 s each, 0.07 s apart in order, node 0 first at 2.8, nodes 1-3 each 0.25 s later) from the tray to cl.slot(n, i); chips 9-12 turn red + solid when they land (they hang below the card); 4.4 every node gets a red ring (cl.set ring 'red', ringK ramp), a red D5.tag 'no room' pops under each overflow row (y 478). 5.0-5.4 all 48 copies and the rings shrink and fade out (s 1 -> 0.6, o 1 -> 0) together. 5.4-7.6 SPLIT: the 12 tray chips fly to their node: orders 1-3 to cl.slot(0, 0..2), 4-6 to node 1, 7-9 node 2, 10-12 node 3 (D5.layout('part')), 0.12 s apart, arc -40; the tags P1-P4 pop at 6.8; 7.4 green rings pop on the four nodes and the tray tag fades. 8.2-10.4 FOLLOWERS: 12 dashed blue chips (dashed: true) fly from each leader chip to cl.slot(D5.followerNode(p), 3..5) (node p + 1 holds the followers of partition p: node 1 holds followers of 10-12), 0.1 s apart, arc 30; the legend appears at 8.0; at 10.2 the green 'x of 8' tags pop reading '6 of 8' (D5.layout('both')[n].length and D5.SPLIT.cap). 10.6-11.8 hold.

END STATE: four green nodes, each with three solid and three dashed chips, '6 of 8' tags, legend visible.

title: Each partition owns
a range of keys
caps: Give each node a range of sorted keys.
Okafor sits between N and S, so it goes to node 3.
Ask for Khan to Mills: one node has them all.
Neighbouring keys sit together.
scenes.spec:
IDEA (lesson ds5-range 5.2): key-range partitioning gives each partition a continuous range of SORTED keys (like encyclopaedia volumes). To place a key you find the range that holds it; neighbouring keys stay together, so a range query reads one node. Data: D5.RANGES ['A-F','G-M','N-S','T-Z'], D5.NAME_NODES (surnames per node, sorted), D5.NEW_NAME 'Okafor' (D5.nodeOfName -> node 2, D5.insertAt(D5.NAME_NODES[2], 'Okafor') = 1), D5.QUERY = D5.rangeQuery('Khan','Mills') = {nodes: [1], hits: Khan, Lewis (Morgan is outside)}. COLOURS (whole video): blue = the data and what we ask about (keys, orders, records, the query, the search word); green = even, fits, cheap, healthy (a fair node, a tick, 'asked 1 node'); red = overload, overflow, hot spot, expensive ('asked 4 nodes', 'moved 9 of 12'); orange = attention and things in motion (the new node, the key being placed, a pointer, a hashed number, a stolen partition); purple = the routing rule or lookup table (range tags, hash ranges, the hash box, the index, 'key mod N', the size limit); grey = neutral (idle nodes, empty slots, the rest). Every label is 28 px or more; symbols are SVG (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, D5.icon.*), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure). Setup lines every scene starts with: const V = window.VID, D5 = V.d5, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V.

LAYOUT. const cl = D5.cluster(stage, {x: 12, y: 150, n: 4, w: 210, gap: 24, cols: 1, rows: 4, cw: 178, ch: 44, cg: 6}) (card 150-416; tags over the nodes at y 82-140: cl.set(n, {tag: D5.RANGES[n], tagK})). Name chips D5.chip(stage, {text, w: 178, h: 44, tone: 'grey'}) at cl.slot(n, i) for the surnames of D5.NAME_NODES; the 4th slot of A-F, N-S and T-Z is empty (dashed). Key chip 'Okafor' D5.chip({text: 'Okafor', w: 150, h: 48, tone: 'blue', solid: true}) at (468, 36). Pointer: an orange D5.disc size 40 or a small orange chip hopping over the tag positions cl.tagAt(n). Query pill D5.tag(stage, {x: 357, y: 8, text: 'Khan to Mills', tone: 'blue', solid: true, icon: 'search'}). Stat D5.stat(stage, {x: 330, y: 470, w: 276, h: 80, label: 'nodes asked', tone: 'green'}) reading '1'.

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.2 nodes pop (0.1 s apart) with their tags and names; 1.4-1.9 Okafor pops. 2.8-4.2 the orange pointer hops tag to tag (A-F at 2.9, G-M at 3.4, N-S at 3.9, 0.35 s each hop, E.inOut); a tag the pointer leaves flashes red briefly (no match), the N-S tag turns green solid at 3.9 and node 2 gets a blue ring. 4.3-5.5 Okafor flies (arc -30) into cl.slot(2, 1) while Patel and Quinn slide down one slot (cl.slot(2, 2), cl.slot(2, 3)); Okafor turns grey (tone 'grey') as it lands and the ring fades. 6.4 Okafor is gone, the query pill pops (6.4-6.9); 6.9-7.8 a blue arrow (D5.link from the pill bottom to cl.top(1) minus 60 px) draws on, node 1 (G-M) gets a blue ring, Khan and Lewis turn solid blue (hits from D5.QUERY.hits), Morgan stays grey; 8.3-8.8 the green stat pops reading D5.QUERY.nodes.length. 9.0-11.8 hold (a gentle pulse of the two hit chips, flash 9.2-9.8).

END STATE: G-M node ringed blue with Khan and Lewis lit, the other nodes untouched, 'nodes asked 1' in green.

title: Keyed by time,
every write hits one node
caps: Key by time: each node owns some hours.
It is afternoon, so new writes go to 12 to 17.
Write after write, all on the same node.
One hot spot while three nodes sit idle.
scenes.spec:
IDEA (lesson ds5-range 5.2): with sorted keys, if the key order follows the arrival order (a timestamp) every new write goes to the node that owns 'now': a write hot spot while the others idle. Data: D5.HOURS ['00-05','06-11','12-17','18-23'], D5.WRITES (6 timestamps 14:02 ... 14:50), D5.nodeOfTime -> 2 for every one, D5.loadAt(k) = writes per node after k writes (D5.loadAt(6) = [0,0,6,0]). COLOURS (whole video): blue = the data and what we ask about (keys, orders, records, the query, the search word); green = even, fits, cheap, healthy (a fair node, a tick, 'asked 1 node'); red = overload, overflow, hot spot, expensive ('asked 4 nodes', 'moved 9 of 12'); orange = attention and things in motion (the new node, the key being placed, a pointer, a hashed number, a stolen partition); purple = the routing rule or lookup table (range tags, hash ranges, the hash box, the index, 'key mod N', the size limit); grey = neutral (idle nodes, empty slots, the rest). Every label is 28 px or more; symbols are SVG (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, D5.icon.*), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure). Setup lines every scene starts with: const V = window.VID, D5 = V.d5, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V.

LAYOUT. const cl = D5.cluster(stage, {x: 12, y: 200, n: 4, w: 210, gap: 24, cols: 2, rows: 3, cw: 88, ch: 44, cg: 6}) (card 200-416; purple hour tags over each node via cl.set(n, {tag: D5.HOURS[n]})). Clock: orange solid D5.tag(stage, {x: 408, y: 40, w: 120, text, tone: 'orange', solid: true, icon: 'client'}) whose text is the timestamp of the write being sent (it reads '14:00' first). Six write chips D5.chip(stage, {text: D5.WRITES[i], w: 88, h: 44, tone: 'blue'}) flying from (468, 80) to cl.slot(2, i). Per node a meter D5.meter(stage, {x: cl.box(n).x + 15, y: 440, w: 180, tone: 'green'}) with k = D5.loadAt(done)[n] / 6, and a 28 px count D5.text under it (y 480: '0', '0', '6', '0'); tags 'idle' (grey) at y 480 replace the counts on nodes 0, 1, 3 at 8.8 and a red solid tag 'hot spot' (D5.tag, x 520, y 480 region, centred under node 2) pops at 8.5.

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.2 nodes (tags, meters) pop; clock pops 1.4 reading '14:00'. 3.2 + 0.85 i (i = 0..5): write i leaves the clock (clock text = D5.WRITES[i]), flies 0.6 s (arc -40, E.inOut) to cl.slot(2, i) (2 columns x 3 rows: all six fit), node 2's meter then ramps to its new value over 0.3 s; node 2 turns tone 'red' (cl.set tone) once the 4th write has landed (6.0) and its meter turns red; nodes 0, 1, 3 stay grey and their meters stay empty. 8.5-9.0 the 'hot spot' tag pops, 8.8-9.3 the three 'idle' tags pop. 9.4-12.4 hold with a gentle pulse of the red node (flash 9.6-10.4).

END STATE: node 12-17 red with six chips and a full red meter; three grey nodes with empty meters and 'idle'.

title: Hash the key,
spread the load
caps: A hash turns a key into a number.
Each node owns a range of hash values.
Keys arrive in order but land all over.
Eight keys: two on every node.
scenes.spec:
IDEA (lesson ds5-hash 5.3): a hash function turns a key into a number; each node owns a range of HASH values instead of a range of keys; consecutive keys get unrelated hashes, so they land on different nodes and the load spreads evenly. Data: D5.ARRIVALS = [{id, hash, node}] for keys 101..108 = hash 11, 2, 14, 6, 9, 0, 13, 4 on nodes 2, 0, 3, 1, 2, 0, 3, 1 (0-based), D5.HASH_RANGES ['0-3','4-7','8-11','12-15']; two keys per node at the end (asserted). COLOURS (whole video): blue = the data and what we ask about (keys, orders, records, the query, the search word); green = even, fits, cheap, healthy (a fair node, a tick, 'asked 1 node'); red = overload, overflow, hot spot, expensive ('asked 4 nodes', 'moved 9 of 12'); orange = attention and things in motion (the new node, the key being placed, a pointer, a hashed number, a stolen partition); purple = the routing rule or lookup table (range tags, hash ranges, the hash box, the index, 'key mod N', the size limit); grey = neutral (idle nodes, empty slots, the rest). Every label is 28 px or more; symbols are SVG (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, D5.icon.*), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure). Setup lines every scene starts with: const V = window.VID, D5 = V.d5, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V.

LAYOUT. Queue: eight blue chips D5.chip(stage, {text: '101'..'108', w: 64, h: 44}) centre x = 50 + 72 i, y 40. Hash box D5.hashBox(stage, {x: 700, y: 8, w: 190, h: 100}) (purple, # icon). The hashed number: an orange D5.disc size 56. Hash cells: const nc = D5.cells(stage, {n: 16, per: 4, centres: [117, 351, 585, 819], y: 190, w: 46, h: 46, gap: 4, tone: 'purple'}) (values 0-15, four above each node, so each node's range 0-3 / 4-7 / 8-11 / 12-15 is literally above it; cell i centre = nc.mid(i)). Nodes: const cl = D5.cluster(stage, {x: 12, y: 290, n: 4, w: 210, gap: 24, cols: 2, rows: 1, cw: 64, ch: 44, cg: 8}) (card 290-406; key chips land on cl.slot(node, 0..1)). End: four green discs D5.disc size 48 text '2' at the top-right corner of each card.

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.2 nodes, cells, hash box and the key queue pop. KEY 101 slowly (1.4-4.2): 1.4-2.0 the chip flies (arc -30) into the hash box (it shrinks to s 0.4 and fades while hb.set({pulse: flash}) swells the box); 2.2-2.8 the orange disc '11' (D5.ARRIVALS[0].hash) pops out under the box and flies (arc 20) to cell 11, which turns orange solid and rings; 3.0-3.8 the key chip (re-created at the cell, blue) drops from cell 11 into node 2 slot 0, the cell fades back to purple. KEYS 102-103 (4.2-5.4 and 5.4-6.4): same sequence, 0.5 s shorter each. KEYS 104-108 (6.4-10.0): 0.72 s each (queue chip -> box -> disc -> cell -> node); the disc and cell step can be overlapped. 10.0-10.8 each node pops its green ring and the green '2' disc. 10.8-12.8 hold.

END STATE: eight blue chips, two in every node, four green rings with '2' discs, all cells back to purple.

title: Hashing scatters
range queries
caps: The same 16 users, laid out two ways.
Now ask for ids 101 to 104.
Key ranges: all four are on one node.
Hash: they are on four different nodes.
scenes.spec:
IDEA (lesson ds5-hash 5.3): hashing buys an even spread but throws away key order, so a range query (neighbouring ids) must ask many nodes; key ranges answer it from one node. Data: D5.RNODES (key-range layout: 101-104 | 105-108 | 109-112 | 113-116) and D5.HNODES (hash layout: [102,106,111,115] [104,108,109,113] [101,105,112,116] [103,107,110,114]); D5.RQ = {ids: [101..104], range: [0], hash: [0,1,2,3]} (nodes a query for these ids must ask). COLOURS (whole video): blue = the data and what we ask about (keys, orders, records, the query, the search word); green = even, fits, cheap, healthy (a fair node, a tick, 'asked 1 node'); red = overload, overflow, hot spot, expensive ('asked 4 nodes', 'moved 9 of 12'); orange = attention and things in motion (the new node, the key being placed, a pointer, a hashed number, a stolen partition); purple = the routing rule or lookup table (range tags, hash ranges, the hash box, the index, 'key mod N', the size limit); grey = neutral (idle nodes, empty slots, the rest). Two stacked clusters, each const mk = (y) => D5.cluster(stage, {x: 12, y, n: 4, w: 210, gap: 24, cols: 2, rows: 2, cw: 64, ch: 44, cg: 8, headH: 52}) (card height 164): top = mk(70) (70-234), bottom = mk(396) (396-560). Row labels: purple D5.tag(stage, {x: 12, y: 0, text: 'key ranges'}) and D5.tag(stage, {x: 12, y: 326, text: 'hash'}). title: Search by colour:
ask every partition
caps: Each partition indexes only its own cars.
Search for red cars.
Any partition may hold one, so ask all three.
Gather the answers into one list.
scenes.spec:
IDEA (lesson ds5-index 5.4): a secondary index searches by something that is not the key (colour). Index BY DOCUMENT (local): every partition indexes only its own documents, so a search cannot tell which partitions hold a match and is sent to ALL of them and the answers are gathered (scatter-gather); a write touches one partition. Data: 12 used cars D5.CARS (D5.carText(id) -> '4 red'), D5.DOCS = [[1,4,7,10],[2,5,8,11],[3,6,9,12]] (document partition = id mod 3), D5.search('red') = {ids: [1,4,6,9,12], local: [[1,4],[],[6,9,12]], askedDoc: 3}: partition 2 holds NO red car but still has to be asked. COLOURS (whole video): blue = the data and what we ask about (keys, orders, records, the query, the search word); green = even, fits, cheap, healthy (a fair node, a tick, 'asked 1 node'); red = overload, overflow, hot spot, expensive ('asked 4 nodes', 'moved 9 of 12'); orange = attention and things in motion (the new node, the key being placed, a pointer, a hashed number, a stolen partition); purple = the routing rule or lookup table (range tags, hash ranges, the hash box, the index, 'key mod N', the size limit); grey = neutral (idle nodes, empty slots, the rest). Every label is 28 px or more; symbols are SVG (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, D5.icon.*), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure). Setup lines every scene starts with: const V = window.VID, D5 = V.d5, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V.

LAYOUT. const cl = D5.cluster(stage, {x: 12, y: 150, n: 3, w: 288, gap: 24, cols: 2, rows: 2, cw: 134, ch: 44, cg: 4, h: 246, names: ['Partition 1','Partition 2','Partition 3']}) (card 150-396). Car chips D5.chip(stage, {text: D5.carText(id), w: 134, h: 44, tone: 'grey'}) at cl.slot(n, j) for D5.DOCS. Under the chips of each card (card y + 172) a purple D5.tag(stage, {x: card.x + 20, y: card.y + 172, w: 248, text: 'own index'}) that later reads 'red: 1, 4' / 'red: none' / 'red: 6, 9, 12' (build the text from D5.search('red').local). Search pill D5.tag(stage, {x: 400, y: 20, text: 'red', tone: 'blue', solid: true, icon: 'search'}). Three blue arrows: const link = D5.link(L5.svg(stage), {x: 468, y: 82}, {x: cl.top(n).x, y: cl.top(n).y - 6}, 'blue'). Answer strip: tag D5.tag(stage, {x: 12, y: 462, text: 'answer', tone: 'blue'}) and five blue chips (ids 1, 4, 6, 9, 12; w 56) at centre x 220 + 72 i, y 491. Stat D5.stat(stage, {x: 612, y: 452, w: 312, h: 72, label: 'asked', tone: 'red'}) reading '3 of 3'.

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.2 cards and car chips pop (0.04 s apart), 0.8 the 'own index' tags. 3.4-4.0 the search pill pops. 6.0-7.0 the three arrows draw on together and the three cards get red rings (every partition is asked); 7.0 the stat pops. 7.0-8.2 the index tags change text to the local results, the red cars turn solid blue (D5.search('red').ids), partition 2's tag reads 'red: none'. 8.8-10.4 the matching chips fly (arc 20, 0.12 s apart, in id order) down to the answer strip. 10.4-11.4 hold.

END STATE: three red-ringed partitions, five lit chips collected in the answer strip, red stat '3 of 3'.

title: Split the index by term:
one read, wider writes
caps: Or split the index itself, by term.
A search reads just one index partition.
Save a blue mini: two index partitions change.
Cheap reads, dearer writes.
scenes.spec:
IDEA (lesson ds5-index 5.4): index BY TERM (global): the index itself is split by word. A search reads ONE index partition, which lists the ids; a write may touch SEVERAL index partitions because one document has several terms. Data: D5.TERMS ['blue','ford','green','kia','mini','red'], D5.idxPart(term) = index / 2 (Index 1: blue, ford; Index 2: green, kia; Index 3: mini, red), D5.postings(term) = ids, D5.search('red') = {idx: 2, ids: [1,4,6,9,12], fetch: [0, 2]}; D5.NEWCAR = [13, 'blue', 'mini'] and D5.write(D5.NEWCAR) = {docPart: 0, idxParts: [0, 2], byDoc: 1, byTerm: 3}. COLOURS (whole video): blue = the data and what we ask about (keys, orders, records, the query, the search word); green = even, fits, cheap, healthy (a fair node, a tick, 'asked 1 node'); red = overload, overflow, hot spot, expensive ('asked 4 nodes', 'moved 9 of 12'); orange = attention and things in motion (the new node, the key being placed, a pointer, a hashed number, a stolen partition); purple = the routing rule or lookup table (range tags, hash ranges, the hash box, the index, 'key mod N', the size limit); grey = neutral (idle nodes, empty slots, the rest). Every label is 28 px or more; symbols are SVG (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, D5.icon.*), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure). Setup lines every scene starts with: const V = window.VID, D5 = V.d5, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V.

LAYOUT. Index cards: const ic = D5.cluster(stage, {x: 12, y: 76, n: 3, w: 288, gap: 24, cols: 1, rows: 1, cw: 250, ch: 44, h: 170, slots: false, icon: false, tone: 'purple', names: ['Index 1','Index 2','Index 3']}) (card 76-246); in each two D5.text lines (tone 'purple', x = card.x + 20, y = card.y + 62 and + 112) 'blue: 2 5 8 11' ... built from D5.postings (colon, no arrow glyph). Document cards: const dc = D5.cluster(stage, {x: 12, y: 340, n: 3, w: 288, gap: 24, cols: 5, rows: 1, cw: 48, ch: 44, cg: 6, slots: true, names: ['Cars 1','Cars 2','Cars 3'], icon: true}) (card 340-456; five slots per card, the fifth is free for car 13), chips D5.chip({text: String(id), w: 48, h: 44}) at dc.slot(n, j) for D5.DOCS. Search pill D5.tag(stage, {x: 568, y: 4, text: 'red', tone: 'blue', solid: true, icon: 'search'}) above Index 3, arrow D5.link(L5.svg(stage), pill bottom, ic.top(2)). New car: D5.chip(stage, {text: '13 blue mini', w: 190, h: 48, tone: 'blue', solid: true}) at (110, 520). Two stats at y 500: D5.stat({x: 12 (then 484), y: 500, w: 440, h: 72}) labels 'search reads' (green, '1') and 'write updates' (orange, '2').

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.4 index cards (with lines) and document cards pop. 3.6-4.0 search pill; 4.0-4.8 the arrow draws on and Index 3 gets a blue ring, its 'red:' line turns blue (tone via D5.text), the green stat pops '1'. 5.2-6.4 the five ids fly (copy chips, arc 20) from the red line to their cars: 1, 4 in Cars 1, 6, 9, 12 in Cars 3 (dc.slot), turning those chips blue (D5.search('red').fetch = [0, 2]). 6.6 the blue rings fade. 7.0-7.8 the new car chip pops at left and flies to dc.slot(0, 4) (D5.write(D5.NEWCAR).docPart); 8.0-9.2 two small '13' chips fly (arc -20) from the car to the 'blue' line in Index 1 and the 'mini' line in Index 3 (idxParts [0, 2]) and the lines gain ' 13' (text 'blue: 2 5 8 11 13', 'mini: 3 6 8 12 13'); those two cards get orange rings and the stat 'write updates' pops reading D5.write(D5.NEWCAR).idxParts.length. 9.6-11.8 hold.

END STATE: two orange-ringed index cards with 13 added, the car in Cars 1, stats '1' (green) and '2' (orange).

title: A new node joins:
move as little as you can
caps: Twelve items on three nodes. A fourth joins.
Hash mod N: N changed, so 9 of 12 keys move.
Fixed partitions: it steals 3 whole ones.
Three moves instead of nine.
scenes.spec:
IDEA (lesson ds5-rebalance 5.5): when a node joins, move as little data as possible. The trap 'node = key mod N': N changes, so the answer changes for most keys (3 -> 4 nodes moves 9 of 12). Fixed partitions: create many partitions (here 12), the new node steals WHOLE partitions from the fullest nodes (3 of 12) and the key-to-partition assignment never changes. Data: D5.MOD = {keys: 0..11, from: k mod 3, to: k mod 4, moved: [3..11] (9 keys), stay: [0,1,2]}; D5.FIXED = {own0: p mod 3, steals: [{p: 9, from: 0}, {p: 10, from: 1}, {p: 11, from: 2}], nodes1: [[0,3,6],[1,4,7],[2,5,8],[9,10,11]], moved: 3}; D5.slotsOf(list, node). Same event, two rules, side by side. COLOURS (whole video): blue = the data and what we ask about (keys, orders, records, the query, the search word); green = even, fits, cheap, healthy (a fair node, a tick, 'asked 1 node'); red = overload, overflow, hot spot, expensive ('asked 4 nodes', 'moved 9 of 12'); orange = attention and things in motion (the new node, the key being placed, a pointer, a hashed number, a stolen partition); purple = the routing rule or lookup table (range tags, hash ranges, the hash box, the index, 'key mod N', the size limit); grey = neutral (idle nodes, empty slots, the rest). Every label is 28 px or more; symbols are SVG (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, D5.icon.*), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure). Setup lines every scene starts with: const V = window.VID, D5 = V.d5, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V.

LAYOUT. Two clusters of four nodes: const mk = (y) => D5.cluster(stage, {x: 12, y, n: 4, w: 210, gap: 24, cols: 2, rows: 2, cw: 70, ch: 44, cg: 8, headH: 52, names: ['Node A','Node B','Node C','Node D']}) (card height 164): top = mk(76) (76-240), bottom = mk(396) (396-560); node D (index 3) starts as ghost (cl.set(3, {ghost: true})) and joins with ghost false, tone 'orange', ring 'orange'. Top chips D5.chip(stage, {text: String(k), w: 70, h: 44}) for keys 0-11 at the slot of node k mod 3, slot index floor(k / 3) (so node A holds 0,3,6,9); bottom chips text 'P0'..'P11' tone 'grey', same slots (p mod 3, floor(p / 3)). Row labels: purple D5.tag(stage, {x: 12, y: 8, text: 'node = key mod N'}) and a tag 'N = 3' at x 290 (text changes to 'N = 4'); bottom purple D5.tag(stage, {x: 12, y: 328, text: '12 fixed partitions'}). Stats D5.stat(stage, {x: 600, y: 4 and 324, w: 324, h: 64, label: 'moved'}), top red reading '9 of 12', bottom green reading '3 of 12' (counting up).

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.4 both rows (nodes A-C, chips, ghost D) pop; labels 0.8. 2.0-3.0 node D joins in both rows (ghost off, orange ring pop, 'N = 3' flips to 'N = 4' at 2.6). 3.4-6.6 TOP: the 9 chips of D5.MOD.moved turn orange and fly (arc +-40, E.inOut, 0.5 s each, 0.25 s apart, in key order) to the slot of node k mod 4 (sorted by key inside each node; chips 0, 1, 2 stay put), the red counter counts 1..9 as each lands; when done they settle back to blue. 7.4-10.2 BOTTOM: P9, P10, P11 (D5.FIXED.steals, in order) turn orange and fly to node D slots 0, 1, 2 (0.7 s each, 1.0 s apart), the green counter counts 1, 2, 3; each source node is flashed (ring blue 0.4 s). 10.4-11.0 both counters bump. 11.0-13.4 hold.

END STATE: top four nodes with a criss-cross of 12 chips and red '9 of 12'; bottom four nodes with three partitions each and green '3 of 12'.

title: Big partitions split,
small ones merge
caps: Each partition has a size limit: 10 GB.
Data grows: P2 reaches 12 GB, over the limit.
It splits in two, and one half can move node.
Data shrinks: small neighbours merge.
scenes.spec:
IDEA (lesson ds5-rebalance 5.5): with dynamic partitioning a partition that grows past a size limit splits in two (each half can live on a different node); when data shrinks small neighbours merge. Data (GB, run as code): D5.DYN = {limit: 10, start: [6, 8, 4], grown: [10, 12, 8] (+4 each), split: [10, 6, 6, 8] (only P2 > 10 splits, splitAt 1), shrunk: [5, 3, 3, 4] (halved), merged: [5, 6, 4] (neighbours 3 + 3 < 7 merge, mergeAt 1)}. COLOURS (whole video): blue = the data and what we ask about (keys, orders, records, the query, the search word); green = even, fits, cheap, healthy (a fair node, a tick, 'asked 1 node'); red = overload, overflow, hot spot, expensive ('asked 4 nodes', 'moved 9 of 12'); orange = attention and things in motion (the new node, the key being placed, a pointer, a hashed number, a stolen partition); purple = the routing rule or lookup table (range tags, hash ranges, the hash box, the index, 'key mod N', the size limit); grey = neutral (idle nodes, empty slots, the rest). Every label is 28 px or more; symbols are SVG (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, D5.icon.*), never glyphs. Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure). Setup lines every scene starts with: const V = window.VID, D5 = V.d5, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V.

LAYOUT. const cl = D5.cluster(stage, {x: 12, y: 120, n: 3, w: 288, gap: 24, cols: 1, rows: 1, cw: 200, ch: 44, h: 360, slots: false}) (cards 120-480; node centres 156, 468, 780). Tanks: baseline y = cl.box(0).y + cl.h - 24 = 456; const t = D5.tank(stage, {x: centre, y: 456, w: 84, scale: 15, tone: 'blue'}) (height = GB x 15 px, text '<gb> GB'); one tank alone sits at its node centre, two tanks in one node at centre -56 and +56. Names 'P1'..'P4' as 28 px D5.text under the baseline (y 464, inside the card bottom). Limit: const r = D5.rule(stage, {x: 12, y: 456 - 150, w: 912, text: 'limit 10 GB'}) (purple dashed line at 10 GB, label over its right end).

TIMELINE. 0.2-1.2 cards, tanks 6, 8, 4 GB (tank growth from 0, 0.1 s apart) and the limit rule pop. 3.0-4.2 every tank grows by 4 GB together (gb = lerp(D5.DYN.start[i], D5.DYN.grown[i], E.inOut)); the middle tank crosses the line and turns red (tone 'red') at about 3.9, P1 reaches exactly 10 and stays blue. 5.8-6.6 P2 splits: two tanks of D5.DYN.split[1] and [2] = 6 GB (left stays red-to-blue as it shrinks, tone 'blue', a split flash); 6.6-7.8 the right half slides (arc -40) into node 3 beside P3, whose tank is 8 GB, at centre +56 (P3 shifts to -56); names 'P2a' / 'P2b' can be 'P2' / 'P3' with P3 renamed 'P4' (keep the names on screen at 28 px). 8.2-9.3 SHRINK: all tanks halve (gb -> D5.DYN.shrunk) and the two adjacent 3 GB halves slide together and fuse into one 6 GB tank (D5.DYN.merged) in node 2 (the right one leaves node 3). 9.4-10.4 hold.

END STATE: three tanks 5, 6, 4 GB under the limit line, each blue.

Copy the frame of videos/a6/scene-11-recap.js and videos/l5/scene-10-recap.js: kicker 'RECAP' (.v-kicker at x 72, y 74), headline 'Remember' (76 px, x 72, top 108), the Pebble mascot V.mascot('pebble', {size: 168, mood: 'love'}) at x 840, y 38 bobbing, three plain sticker rows (x 72, width 936, height 180, tops 240 / 444 / 648; V.h('div', {class: 'v-card plain c-<tone>'}), edge colours blue / purple / orange), in each row a 340 x 140 pictogram on the left (div at left 16, top 10, transform scale(1.1), origin 0 0; draw with L5.svg(pic, 340, 140) and D5 helpers, which take any parent) and the bold label (36 px, up to two lines of at most 22 characters, from x 440, vertically centred) on the right. At the bottom, centred at y 904, one solid blue tag (34 px, 'v-tag solid c-blue') 'Next: Workshop 5.W'. Rows slide in at 0.8 / 1.9 / 3.0 (0.5 s, label 0.15 s later); each pictogram starts 0.4 s after its row and PLAYS ONCE then HOLDS its finished state until the end (no loop, no fade-out, no reset icon); all three are finished by 6.6; the call to action pops at 5.4-6.0 (scale 0.8 -> 1, E.pop); in the last 2 s only Pebble's bob moves. No captions. Numbers in pictograms come from D5 data asserted at build time (12 items, 3 steals: D5.FIXED.moved, D5.RQ.range / D5.RQ.hash lengths 1 and 4).

helpers:
FILES: videos/d5/common.js (pure data and algorithms, no DOM, every number asserted at page load: D5.same throws a clear Error), common-2.js (chip, tag, stat, disc, fly, appear, seq, icons), common-3.js (cluster, meter, tank, rule, hashBox, cells, text, link). Everything hangs off window.VID.d5; scenes start with const V = window.VID, D5 = V.d5, L5 = V.l5. videos/ds-5.html loads engine.js, cards.js, l5/common.js, then d5/common.js, common-2.js, common-3.js, then scene-01 ... scene-11, audio/ds-5.js. READ THE API COMMENTS AT THE TOP OF EACH FILE FIRST: they are the contract. All draw calls are pure: call them every frame from update(t) with everything you want to see; nothing is remembered between frames.

A. DATA (common.js): D5.SPLIT / D5.layout(mode) / D5.followerNode / D5.lost; D5.RANGES / NAME_NODES / NEW_NAME / nodeOfName / insertAt / rangeQuery / QUERY; D5.HOURS / WRITES / nodeOfTime / loadAt; D5.HASH_RANGES / hashOf / hNode / rNode / KEYS8 / ARRIVALS / HNODES / RNODES / askedNodes / RQ; D5.CARS / carText / docPart / DOCS / TERMS / idxPart / postings / search / NEWCAR / write; D5.MOD / FIXED / slotsOf / DYN; tools D5.same / sum / count / sorted / pct / ids.
B. DRAWING (common-2.js): D5.chip(parent, {text, tone, w, h, fs, radius, lip}) -> {set({x, y (CENTRE), s, sx, r, o, tone, text, solid, ghost, dashed, ring, ringK, ringDash}), w, h}; D5.chipW(text); D5.tag(parent, {x, y, text, tone, solid, fs, h, w, icon}) -> set({text, tone, solid, k, x, y, s, o}); D5.tagW(text); D5.stat(parent, {x, y, w, h, label, tone}) -> set({text, tone, solid, bump, k, o, x, y}); D5.disc(parent, {x, y (centre), size, text, tone}) -> set({text, tone, solid, k, x, y, s, o}); D5.fly(a, b, k, {arc}) -> {x, y}; D5.appear(k) -> {s, o}; D5.seq(t, t0, step, dur, i); D5.lerp2; D5.icon.server / client / hash / search / plus (x, y, size, tone) -> <g> for an L5.svg layer; D5.tone(name); D5.TONES.
C. RIGS (common-3.js): D5.cluster(parent, {x, y, n, w, gap, cols, rows, cw, ch, cg, pad, headH, names, slots, tone, icon, h}) -> {set(i, {tone, k, o, x, y, s, label, ghost, ring, ringK, ringDash, slotsO, tag, tagTone, tagSolid, tagK}), slot(i, j), box(i), mid(i), top(i), bottom(i), tagAt(i), n, w, h, ...} (four nodes: w 210, gap 24, x 12, centres 117 351 585 819; three nodes: w 288, gap 24, centres 156 468 780); D5.meter(parent, {x, y, w, h, tone, mark}) -> set({k, tone, o, x, y}); D5.tank(parent, {x (centre), y (baseline), w, scale, tone}) -> set({gb, tone, text, o, x, y, solid, dashed, s}); D5.rule(parent, {x, y, w, text, tone}) -> set({k, o, y, tone}); D5.hashBox(parent, {x, y, w, h, text}) -> set({k, o, pulse, x, y, s}); D5.cells(parent, {n, per, centres, y, w, h, gap, tone, texts}) -> {set(i, {..chip fields, dx, dy}), mid(i)}; D5.text(parent, {x, y, text, tone, fs, w, align}) -> set({text, tone, k, o, x, y, bold}); D5.link(L5.svg(stage), a, b, tone, opt) -> (k, o) => draws an arrow on.
NOTES FOR SCENE AUTHORS: (1) chips use x, y = CENTRE; tags, stats, cards use x, y = TOP-LEFT; offsets in set() are from where the thing was placed. (2) Chip widths: a 3-digit id needs w >= 60, a 5-char time w >= 88, 'Okafor' w >= 120, '10 green' w >= 134 at 28 px. (3) A cluster tag must be passed to cl.set every frame (omit it and it hides). (4) Rings are 9 px outside the card: leave room. (5) Colour roles are fixed for the whole video (see outline).
